name: NTP Drift Breaks Authentication
description: An ESXi host loses sync with the corporate NTP fleet and the VMs running on it slowly drift forward by ~6 minutes. JWT validation starts failing with 'token used before nbf', Kerberos tickets get rejected by AD, and the affected app servers can no longer authenticate to the database.
reasoning: Two app servers behind nginx talk to a Postgres that authenticates via Kerberos. The drift is invisible until token signatures stop validating; it manifests as auth-only failures while ICMP/networking still works.

nodes.label: WIN-APP-IAD-09
nodes.notes: Windows Server 2019 VM on host esx-iad-12.

narrative.text: Baseline traffic, no anomalies, app servers in sync.
esx-iad-12 ntpd dies silently after a guest tools update. Drift accumulates.
Drift > 5 min. JWT validation: 'JsonWebTokenError: jwt issued in the future'.
Kerberos auth to PG fails: 'Clock skew too great (KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW)'.
Auth-only failures while ping still succeeds — operators chase the wrong layer for 20 min.
An old runbook is dug up; ntpdate -u corp-ntp.acme.local fixes drift in seconds.
Apps recover, AD-bound sessions re-issue successfully.
Postmortem: Telegraf drift metric was scraped but never alerted.
